name: Structure-driven Legal Knowledge Graph and Retrieval Benchmark for German Statute Law
description: Resource accompanying the paper Verifiable Retrieval for Legal Reasoning through Structure-driven Knowledge Graph (RAGE-KG 2026, co-located with ISWC 2026). ## Contents - Statutory knowledge graph (codes_graph.pkl, codes_graph.json): 168,469 nodes and 240,507 edges over 58 German federal codes, in an eight-level typed hierarchy from root to Buchstabe. 22,253 edges are intra-code cross-references derived from in-statute citation tagging.- Six chunk corpora at the Buchstabe (101,614 chunks), Nummer (98,688), Satz (80,174), Absatz (42,573) and paragraph (15,110) levels, plus a fixed-width 100-word control condition. Each corpus is a complete covering of the statute text.- Evaluation results: 30 JSON files covering five embedders across six chunking granularities, with depth-stratified recall, precision, and Token Efficiency Ratio.- Retrieval indices: top-k chunk identifiers per case for KaLM-Embedding-Gemma3-12B.- Case manifest (case_manifest.jsonl, 3.5 MB): the identifiers and source URLs of the 12,037 Bundesgerichtshof decisions forming the evaluation set, with the 139,260 gold citations parsed from them into normalised hierarchy tuples. ## Court decision text is not includedThis deposit distributes the structure of the resource, not the text of the decisions it is evaluated against. German court decisions are free of copyright under section 5(1) UrhG, which names Entscheidungen explicitly.
